text: Rule 3 says runs-left appears only in the criteria table with a "not interpretable" note, but that table also marks runs-left "Passed true" (326.6254, interval [292.0959, 359.6092]) next to a NEGATIVE verdict; a non-programmer could read the green pass as partial success. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Render the "Passed" column for the model-based criteria as "passed, but overridden by failed Brier criterion", or hide the pass flag for runs-left and the negative control, and state which criterion drove the NEGATIVE.

The negative control (0.9567 realized flagged-send success, interval [0.9559, 0.9748]) is marked passed and reads like a high success rate; with sends selected, this invites the reading "sends are 96% safe, so the model works". The spec gives it no plain-language gloss. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Add a fixed caption to each criterion row saying what it checks and that passing it does not rescue the verdict.

The headline Brier gap is -0.0001 against constant (model 0.0354, constant 0.0355, outs-only 0.0355) with interval [-0.0003, 0.0005] spanning zero. The spec's "one-sentence meaning" could say "no better than a constant", but a negative sign may be read as "model slightly better". Hover-for-full-value does not address this. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Show the interval beside every difference and state in text that an interval spanning zero means no demonstrated improvement.

The default decision chart shows "observed send success and break-even p*". Sends are selected, so observed success is conditional on a selection process, and the source says positive estimates are upper-bound-style and the hold counterfactual is extrapolated. The spec has no caveat on the non-model default columns, so an analyst could still use the break-even comparison as a send/hold rule by hand. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Put the selection and extrapolation caveat on the decision chart itself, and add a banner that cell-level rates are not a send/hold policy.

A negative result may be over-read as "send/hold doesn't matter" or "the Cubs are optimal". The source says only that this model, with a reduced covariate set (2025 SENT_OUT 67 against 140 required), did not beat baselines. Reduced covariates and low 2025 support are not among the spec's required caveats. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Require a "Why NEGATIVE does not mean no effect" panel covering reduced covariates, the support threshold of 0.2529, and 199 of 2329 holds (0.0854) below support.

The Cubs descriptive figures (flagged holds 54 in 2025 "in-sample" vs 62 in 2026; runs left 11.6591 vs 13.4059) are marked "descriptive only, no significance claim" in the source. The spec does not say that label must travel with them, and the Cubs case may be read as evidence of lost runs. The R001 Cubs case has the same risk. CITE: sendhold-verdict, r001-assessment
Make "descriptive only; does not evaluate Cubs decisions" a mandatory inline label on every Cubs figure.

The R001 pages risk over-reading in the other direction. "Early stop" with 12-23 positives against a minimum of 30 means the primary test was not run, not that the model failed. The exploratory result (model M roughly ties B0; 2024 AUROC difference -0.016, interval -0.049 to 0.014) is not a pre-registered negative. The spec's three-way NEGATIVE/PARTIAL/EXPLORATORY vocabulary does not clearly separate "not testable" from "tested and failed". CITE: r001-assessment
Add an explicit status "NOT TESTED (early stop)" distinct from NEGATIVE, using the source wording COMPLETE_NEGATIVE only for the run outcome.

The statement that the 2025 holdout is untouched and available for one confirmatory test could prompt readers to treat further tests as likely to succeed. The spec does not say whether this will be displayed, and "repeated practical use: unproven" is easy to omit. CITE: r001-assessment
Show the "repeated practical use: unproven" line verbatim on the overview.

Fidelity tests only compare tagged numbers against source JSON. They would not catch untagged numbers, prose that contradicts the verdict, a verdict string altered consistently in both export and render, or a misleading ordering. Because the export copies values with the same pipeline that produces the page, the test is not independent of the implementation, and the source evidence is itself marked independent_of_implementation false. CITE: sendhold-verdict, r001-assessment
Add a test that fails if any numeric text node lacks a data-src tag, and a golden check of the verdict strings against the published markdown, kept outside the export code.

The spec reads research/*.json, but the evidence supplied is markdown summaries (e.g. FACT/INFERENCE lines). Whether the JSON carries the same labels, such as low_n, and the verbatim INFERENCE text, is unknown. Rule 5 (keep labels verbatim) may not be satisfiable from JSON alone. CITE: sendhold-verdict
json_source_label_coverage

The guard test "no model values visible by default" checks default state only. It would miss model values reachable through URL parameters, print view, or a toggle state persisted across pages; hover and focus tooltips with full values could also expose model numbers. Hidden-by-CSS values may still be read by screen readers.
Test that model values are absent from the DOM (not just hidden) until the toggle is used, including in the accessibility tree, and that the toggle resets on page load.

Hover-for-full-value does not work on touch devices, which matters at 375 px; focus alone is not reachable for non-interactive text. The spec mentions keyboard filters but not touch or screen-reader access to full values. Contrast is tested only as a stated goal, with no automated check listed, and the viewport test checks only horizontal page scroll, not table usability or the de-emphasized low_n cells' legibility.
Make full values available via tap-accessible disclosure or a visible "exact" column, and add an automated axe-style check for contrast and table semantics.

The network test checks requests only to the local server, so it would not catch a link to an external site (attribution, terms) or a copied MLB bulk response. The spec says bulk responses stay local under MLBAM terms, but the web/data export of per-play or per-player values might breach this, which the tests do not cover. CITE: r001-assessment
mlbam_terms_compliance_of_exported_values

Scope is large for a first version: four analyses' criteria tables, v1-to-v3 history, hashes, retrieval totals, feasibility reconciliation, run-expectancy table, dark mode, and filters. Hashes and retrieval totals serve auditors, not the stated analyst or coach.
For v1 ship the overview, a verdict page per study, and the About page; defer filters, the model-values toggle, the dark scheme, and method-note hashes.

Extra caveats are missing from the R001 limitations: playing time reflects opportunity as well as talent, there is no WAR or projection-system comparison, thin samples per segment, and the minor-league versus MLB election methods disagree by about 15%. The spec's "what this does not show" list is not tied to these. CITE: r001-assessment
Derive the "what this does not show" list from the published limitations text, and test that each limitation appears on its study page.
user_comprehension_of_verdict_wording
whether_v2_and_ambiguous_analyses_have_same_support_values

Rule 3 hides model values by default, but the "Brier difference to constant" row is the headline negative result and the spec never says whether it stays visible. If the default view shows only observed send success and break-even p*, an analyst may read "observed send success vs p*" as a usable send/hold rule, which is the failed model's decision logic in a different form. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Add a visible banner on the decision chart stating that observed success rates are selected sends only and say nothing about what holds would have done, and that p* comparisons are not a recommendation.

The evidence says positive estimates are "upper-bound-style" because sends are selected and the hold counterfactual is extrapolated. The spec's decision chart (observed send success per cell) has no such caveat, so selection bias is not carried into the default view. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Carry the INFERENCE about selected sends and extrapolated hold counterfactuals into the chart header verbatim, not only on the verdict page.

The negative control (realized flagged-send success 0.9567, passed true) is listed as "Passed: true" in a table whose overall verdict is NEGATIVE. A non-programmer may read "true" as good and miss that the primary criterion (Brier) failed. Two of four criteria pass, and the spec only says the verdict comes first, not how per-row pass/fail is explained. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Render Passed as text ("Met" / "Not met") with a one-line note that the verdict is decided by the pre-registered rule, not by counting passes.

Calibration slope passed with interval [-0.2065, 1.7621], which is extremely wide. Showing "Passed" without the interval's width could mislead. Rounding rules (rule 1) do not require showing intervals alongside point values. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Require every point estimate to display its published interval adjacent, and flag intervals that include zero or span implausible ranges.

A negative result can be over-read in two directions: "send/hold has no value" (the Brier difference interval [-0.0003, 0.0005] is tiny and includes zero, so the test showed no detectable gain, not proven absence) and "the model is fine at some level." The spec's one-sentence meaning is not specified, so wording is unreviewed. A written template is needed. CITE: sendhold-verdict
exact_plain_language_verdict_wording

The v3 analysis used a reduced covariate set (67 SENT_OUT in 2025 against 140 required), meaning the model was underpowered by design. The spec lists "covariate coverage" under Data but not as a verdict-level caveat. A reader could conclude the full model was tested and failed. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Surface "reduced covariate set; 67 of 140 required" in the verdict panel.

The evidence shows v3 labels are primary and v2 pre-registered is separate, and both are NEGATIVE. The spec shows both, but the v3 label definition was adopted after v2 pre-registration. Without explaining the change, readers may see v3 as post hoc. The "v1 to v3 history" sits in Method notes, far from the verdict. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Put a one-line note under the verdict panel linking to the label-definition history.

199 of 2329 holds (0.0854) fell below the propensity support threshold, and "flagged holds" 1533 versus "assessed holds" 2130 are easily confused. The spec lists flagged holds as model-based but gives no definitions, so a coach could read "flagged holds" as "holds we should have sent." CITE: sendhold-verdict
Add a glossary with hover/focus definitions for flagged, assessed, support threshold and runs left.

The Cubs descriptive figures (flagged holds 54 in-sample for 2025, 62 in 2026; runs left 11.6591 and 13.4059) are labeled descriptive with no significance claim. Rule 3 confines runs-left to the criteria table, but the Cubs case could show these in a card or chart. The spec does not say where they go. Also 2025 is in-sample, so comparing years is invalid. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Exclude Cubs flagged-hold and runs-left values from the Overview and show them only with the in-sample caveat and the failed-model label.

The runs-left criterion is "passed true" with value 326.6 runs, a large number that could be read as an achievable gain. The spec's caveat is a statement, but a large figure in a table remains salient. Consider omitting it. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Show runs-left as "not interpretable" with the value hidden behind the same toggle as other model values, since rule 1 permits hover-only full values.

R001 early-stopped on a primary segment with counts of 12-23 against a minimum of 30. The spec's rule 4 shows n and de-emphasizes low_n cells, but the early-stop means no model was fitted; a reader may expect a model result and take the exploratory table as that result. The EXPLORATORY banner helps, but "roughly ties B0" can be read as "the model works as well as the obvious rule." CITE: r001-assessment
State on the page "No pre-registered test was run; the 2025 holdout is untouched," and phrase the exploratory finding as no evidence of added value.

The Cubs case in R001 (e.g., 3, 1, 6, 0 positives of 14, 12, 10, 8 signings) invites evaluation of Cubs decisions. The source says it only sizes the opportunity and does not evaluate decisions. CITE: r001-assessment
Put that sentence directly above the Cubs table, and avoid per-year signing-versus-positive ratios as a chart.

The source says the two methods separating minor-league from MLB elections disagree by roughly 15%. The spec has no place for this limitation (playing time reflects opportunity as well as talent; no WAR; no projection comparison). Missing caveats weaken "what it does not show." CITE: r001-assessment
Make the "what this does not show" list pull limitations from the source records, not hand-written text.

r001_cubs_signings_vs_segment_counts. The R001 text gives Cubs positives in the no-MLB segment as 1, 0, 1, 0 of 14, 12, 22, 23 league-wide, while elsewhere signings are 14, 12, 10, 8. These are different quantities, and the first list reuses league-wide totals (2021 14, 2022 12) that coincide with Cubs signings. A page could conflate them. CITE: r001-assessment

Fidelity tests compare rendered numbers tagged with data-src against source JSON. They only catch mismatches for tagged numbers. Untagged numbers, prose numbers (the one-sentence meaning, "roughly one player per year") and the labels around a value are not covered. A wrong label next to a correct number passes. Also, the evidence is markdown here while the spec reads research/*.json, so equivalence of the two is UNKNOWN. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Add a test that fails if any digit sequence in rendered text lacks a data-src tag or an allowlist entry, and a test that checks each label-to-pointer mapping.

Guard tests check "no model values visible by default," but the test needs a list of model-value pointers. If the list is hand-maintained, a new model number added later passes silently. The test also misses the Brier model value 0.0354 in the criteria table and the Passed column. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Derive the model-value set from export-time tags (data-class="model") and fail the build if any untagged numeric appears on the send/hold page.
The "verdict precedes any table" test checks DOM order, not screen-reader or small-screen order, and CSS reordering could break it. The test should assert the visual order as well.
Forbid CSS order/position reordering of verdict panels, or assert bounding-box order at 375 px.

The network test checks requests to non-local origins, but the spec does not cover the MLB attribution link or any external link. An outbound link is not a request, but it should be stated. The test also skips when Chromium is unavailable, so CI could pass with no end-to-end coverage.
Make skipped end-to-end tests fail CI for release builds and report the skip count visibly.

Hover-or-focus is the only route to full values, which fails on touch screens at 375 px. The accessibility list omits touch alternatives, zoom/reflow at 400 percent, screen-reader announcement of de-emphasis and the toggle state, reduced motion, and print. Tables scrolling in a container need keyboard focusability and a visible scroll cue.
Provide full values via a tap-accessible disclosure or an expandable detail row, and add a 320 px reflow check.
The "show failed model values" toggle persists state unknown; if it stays on across pages or reloads, a user could land on model values unlabeled. The spec does not say whether it resets.
Reset the toggle on every page load and keep the label attached to each revealed value, not to the toggle.

A static page copying values risks becoming stale. The manifest records the commit, but the spec does not show it on each page. Evidence also shows the experiment is dated and the 2025 holdout remains available for one confirmatory test, so a later result could supersede these verdicts. CITE: r001-assessment
Show commit hash and "as of" date in each page footer, plus a note that later studies may supersede these results.

Scope is large for a first version. Filters on four dimensions, v2 and AMBIGUOUS and fallback-dropped criteria tables, retrieval totals, run-expectancy table, light/dark schemes, and a method history all increase surface for misreading and for test cost. The filters invite slicing small cells into spurious patterns.
For v1, ship Overview, verdict panels, and a static non-filterable decision table; defer filters, the dark scheme, retrieval totals and the run-expectancy table.
audience_comprehension_testing. No evidence shows that a non-programmer analyst can correctly state the verdict after viewing a page.
Add a short comprehension check with two or three target users before release, asking what they would do with the page, and treat any "use the model" answer as a blocker.

json_source_matches_markdown_verdict. Supplied evidence is markdown summaries, so whether research/*.json carries identical figures, fields such as low_n, and the AMBIGUOUS and fallback analyses, is unverified.
mlb_attribution_quote_text. The README quote is not supplied, so compliance of the attribution cannot be judged.

Rule 3 hides model values by default, but the default decision chart still shows "observed send success" and break-even p* beside a send/hold framing. Selected sends are non-random, and the verdict says holds are extrapolated. An analyst could read observed send success as a recommendation to send. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Next to observed send success, add a fixed caveat: "Sends were selected by the club; this is not the success rate of holds or of a different policy." Gate p* behind the same "not for decisions" label unless the source marks it model-free.

The spec never requires a plain statement of what NEGATIVE means. NEGATIVE here is "no demonstrated improvement over a constant baseline", and it is not evidence that sending is wrong or that the model is harmful. The Brier difference to constant is -0.0001 with interval [-0.0003, 0.0005], so it is indistinguishable from zero. An analyst could read NEGATIVE as "the opposite works". CITE: sendhold-verdict
Make the one-sentence verdict meaning a source-keyed, test-checked string: "No measurable improvement over a simple baseline was shown. This does not show the opposite."

The runs-left caveat is confined to the criteria table. In the evidence, the runs-left criterion has Passed=true (326.6 runs, interval [292.1, 359.6]) while the overall verdict is NEGATIVE. A "Passed" column showing true next to a NEGATIVE verdict will mislead readers, and the spec does not say how to present mixed pass/fail rows. The negative-control row (0.9567) is also passed=true but is a sanity check, not support for the model. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Show each criterion's role (gating, diagnostic, control) and state that the verdict follows the failing gating criteria. Render a passed=true row under a failed verdict with a text note rather than a green mark.

The spec's list of caveats is incomplete. It omits that the covariate set was reduced (2025 SENT_OUT 67 against 140 required), that 199 of 2329 holds fall below the support threshold, and that the calibration slope interval [-0.2065, 1.7621] is too wide to interpret. It also omits that the Cubs 2025 flagged holds are in-sample. The spec names low_n cells but not these limits. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Add a mandatory "Limits of this result" block on the send/hold page, populated from the source fields.

v3-primary-vs-v2-verdict. Both are NEGATIVE here, but the spec's treatment of two definitions, plus the AMBIGUOUS and fallback-dropped variants, could show disagreement that the explorer cannot explain. The spec has no rule for disagreement. UNKNOWN: whether the AMBIGUOUS-as-SENT_SAFE and fallback-dropped verdicts agree, because the supplied evidence shows only v3 primary.

The "Exact values" rule conflicts with itself. Hover or focus is the only route to the full values, and touch devices at 375 px have no hover. Keyboard focus on non-interactive text is also unreliable. This is an accessibility and small-screen gap, and it affects whether the fidelity claim can be checked on a phone.
Provide a tap-accessible "show exact values" control, or an expandable details element, in place of hover.

The fidelity tests catch only mismatches between a number and its data-src pointer. They would not catch a wrong pointer, a correct number under the wrong label, a dropped interval, or a verdict mapped to the wrong study. The export also tags numbers by hand, so an untagged number escapes the test. The tests also rely on the same code that wrote the data, and the evidence is marked independent_of_implementation=false. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Add a test that fails if any numeric text node lacks data-src. Add golden-snapshot checks on label-to-pointer pairs, reviewed by a person. Add a check that the interval accompanies every difference shown.

The guard tests check "no model values visible by default" by what the tests anticipate. A new field, such as flagged holds in the Cubs case (62 and 54), could appear without the guard label. The Cubs descriptive rows come from the model's flags and could slip through. CITE: sendhold-verdict
Maintain an allowlist of default-visible pointers, and fail the test on anything outside it. Check the list against the pointers tagged model-derived.

The network test (no requests outside the local server) does not catch misrepresentation. It guards privacy and the no-live-data claim only, and it says nothing about content. The "no live data" claim is also hard-coded as text, and a stale manifest commit would make it false. UNKNOWN: whether the explorer checks the manifest hashes against the source at load time.

R001 can be over-read. The early stop (counts of 12–23 against a minimum of 30) means no model was fitted for the primary test, so it is not evidence that the model fails there. The exploratory tie with B0 (AUROC difference -0.016, interval -0.049 to 0.014) is not proof of equivalence. The Cubs rows (3, 1, 6, 0 positives) can be read as grading Cubs decisions, which the source says they do not do. CITE: r001-assessment
Require a distinct label for "test not run (early stop)" that differs from a failed test, and attach the source's sentence about not evaluating Cubs decisions to every Cubs table.

The R001 outcome measures playing time, not value, and the source says the repeated-practical-use value is unproven. The spec's "what this does not show" list is unspecified, so these limits may be missing. CITE: r001-assessment
the content of the "what this does not show" list, as the spec gives no items.

The scope is too large for a first version. A hash history for v1 to v3, a toggle for failed-model values, four analyses with filters, dark mode, and a per-number hover system could be cut. The core need is the verdict, its meaning, its limits, and the sample sizes.
Version 1 could ship the Overview, the verdict panels, the limits blocks and the About page. Defer the decision-chart filters and the failed-model toggle until the guard tests pass.
The "show failed model values" toggle is itself a risk. Once shown, values may be copied into screenshots without the label. UNKNOWN: whether the label is attached to each value or only to the panel.
Drop the toggle in v1, or watermark the revealed values.

The spec quotes the "usage-restriction quote already in the README", and MLBAM's terms treat bulk responses as non-bulk. The evidence does not show whether published research JSON counts as redistributable. UNKNOWN: legal status of the displayed aggregates.
whether the fidelity tests actually run, since the end-to-end tests skip when Chromium is unavailable. A silent skip could let a build pass with no fidelity check.
Make the skip fail in CI, or record a visible "tests not run" status in the build output.

Rule 3 labels the failed model only on model-derived values, but the spec never labels the observed "send success" and break-even p* columns shown by default in the decision chart. A coach could read these as a usable send/hold lookup, which is the failed model in practice. CITE: sendhold-verdict

The runs-left figure (326.6254, interval [292.0959, 359.6092]) is marked "Passed true" in the criteria table. The spec's caveat helps, but a "Passed" column beside a NEGATIVE verdict can read as contradictory. The table should show why the overall verdict is still NEGATIVE, for example that the Brier criterion failed. CITE: sendhold-verdict

The negative-control value (0.9567, "realized flagged-send success") and the calibration slope (interval [-0.2065, 1.7621]) both pass. A lay reader may see a high success rate and treat it as validation. The spec has no caveat that passing secondary criteria does not offset the failed primary criterion, and that the slope interval is too wide to be informative. CITE: sendhold-verdict

The evidence says any positive estimate is upper-bound-style, because sends are selected and the hold counterfactual is extrapolated. Observed send success from selected sends is therefore biased. The spec does not carry this INFERENCE onto the decision chart page. CITE: sendhold-verdict

A NEGATIVE verdict can be over-read in two ways: as proof that sending or holding has no value, or as proof that the model is wrong. The Brier difference is -0.0001 with interval [-0.0003, 0.0005], which includes zero. The result is "no demonstrated improvement over constant" and not "demonstrably useless". The one-sentence meaning should say this. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Reduced covariate set (2025 SENT_OUT 67 against 140 required) and 199 of 2329 holds below the support threshold are limitations. The spec lists "covariate coverage" under Data but does not require these on the verdict panel. A negative result under a reduced design is weaker evidence than a full-design negative, so it needs to be near the verdict. CITE: sendhold-verdict

The spec lists the v3 primary verdict and the pre-registered v2 verdict, but it does not say that v3 was adopted after v2. Both are NEGATIVE here, so this is low risk, but a future disagreement would need explicit display. UNKNOWN is whether the other analyses (AMBIGUOUS as SENT_SAFE, fallback dropped) agree, since the supplied evidence only covers v3_primary. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Cubs descriptive figures (flagged holds 2025 54 in-sample, 2026 62; runs left 11.6591 and 13.4059) mix an in-sample year with a holdout year and are "descriptive only, no significance claim". The spec has no rule to carry that caveat onto the Cubs display, and a year-over-year comparison would be misleading. CITE: sendhold-verdict

The R001 low-attention segment has positives of 12 to 23 per year, below the pre-registered minimum of 30. A reader may take the early stop as a finding that free agents are not useful. It means only that the test was underpowered by design. The spec should say "not tested" and not "negative". The assessment also records repeated practical use as unproven. CITE: r001-assessment

The exploratory whole-pool result (model M roughly ties B0, 2024 AUROC difference -0.016, interval -0.049 to 0.014) is a tie within the interval and not proof of equivalence. It is also user-requested with no claim. The EXPLORATORY banner needs plain wording on this. CITE: r001-assessment

The Cubs case shows signings and positives (3, 1, 6, 0 reached the threshold) beside league-wide positives. The assessment explicitly says this does not evaluate Cubs decisions, because availability, terms and competing offers are unknown. Without a prominent caveat, an analyst may rate the Cubs' signings as good or bad. CITE: r001-assessment

The outcome is playing time, which reflects opportunity as well as talent. The assessment lists this limitation, along with no WAR, no projection-system comparison, and the minor-league versus MLB election methods disagreeing by about 15%. The spec has no mandatory limitations block on the R001 page, only "its unknowns". CITE: r001-assessment

Fidelity tests compare rendered numbers tagged `data-src` against source JSON. An untagged number, a number in prose, or a tag pointing at the wrong value would escape the test. Tests cannot detect a verdict word that is correct but paired with misleading prose, or a missing caveat inside a different element. The spec needs a test that fails when any digit sequence appears in the DOM without a tag, and a test that each verdict string equals the source verdict.

The guard tests check that the runs-left caveat is present and that model values are hidden by default. They do not check the toggled state: after the toggle is on, the label must remain adjacent to every model value. They also do not check print, copy-paste, or screenshot contexts, where hover text and toggles are lost.

Hover-based access to full values fails on touch screens and for non-pointer users. The spec says "hover or focus", which helps keyboard users. Small-screen touch users have no path, and 375 px is the only narrow width tested. The viewport test checks only horizontal page scroll and not readability, tap-target size, or whether wide tables hide the n column or the low_n text.

The export "never computes new statistics", yet the spec lists some values as "computed" in the browser. The two statements conflict, and the spec does not list the computed values, so the fidelity test has no definition of them. Also, the source files come from the same implementation (`independent_of_implementation` false), so a fidelity test against the JSON verifies copying only and not correctness of the research. CITE: sendhold-verdict

Network test asserts no requests outside the local server. It would not catch a local page loading a stale web/data file, so the manifest hash should be compared at test time with the source files. The "commit X" placeholder needs to be filled from the manifest and not hand-written.

Light and dark schemes, WCAG AA and the Playwright suite, plus per-study pages and filters, are more than a first version needs. The filters over the decision chart invite exploring subgroups. That produces small-n cells and encourages cherry-picking from a model that failed.

Drop the decision-chart filters and the model-values toggle from v1. Show a static verdict page with the criteria table, a "what a negative result means" paragraph, and a limitations block. Defer interactive exploration until a user shows a need.

Add a plain-language line next to the Brier row: "The model did not beat a constant guess; the interval includes zero, so this is no evidence of benefit, not evidence of harm." Add that the passed secondary criteria do not rescue the verdict.
Make a limitations block mandatory per study and test its presence, and add a DOM scan test that flags any untagged number.
whether the decision chart's observed send success and p* columns are derived from selected sends only
whether the other three send/hold analyses agree with v3_primary
whether real analysts or coaches have been shown a prototype and understood the verdicts
which values the spec intends to label "computed"
